newsitem.title: USA: Smith Barney says respects Dade Cty, Fla. decision.
newsitem.headline: Smith Barney says respects Dade Cty, Fla. decision.

text.p: Smith Barney Inc, a unit of Travelers Group Inc, said Tuesday it did not challenge a decision by Dade County, Fla., to remove the firm from an upcoming bond deal because of a pending federal investigation.
The county commission voted 8-1 in February to make Smith Barney senior manager for a $124 million airport revenue refunding bond sale slated for late April.

But Mayor Alex Penelas vetoed the selection earlier this month, saying a Securities and Exchange Commission investigation into Smith Barney's handling of a 1994 Dade County bond issue had "placed a cloud over the firm."
The county commission upheld Penelas' decision on Tuesday.

"While we strongly disagree with the mayor's decision, and believe that the original 8-1 vote by the commission to appoint Smith Barney was in the best interest of the county, we respect their process and did not ask the commission to overturn the veto," said Smith Barney spokeswoman Sally Cates.
"We understand that this decision is limited. It is one transaction and Smith Barney looks forward to being considered for transactions in the future," she said.

The commission accepted the mayor's recommendation to remove Smith Barney from the deal and keep syndicate members Goldman Sach & Co, Bear Stearns & Co and Douglas James Securities Inc. Bear Stearns was chosen senior manager.
